entries.what_happened: The family is one manuscript, 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension' (OpenAI preprint dated 23 September 2026). It claims a proof of the stated theorem: every locally compact, second-countable, Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable topological n-manifold without boundary (n ≥ 1; the 0-dimensional case is trivial) is a Lie group. Its main technical theorem (the 'p-adic exclusion', §5–§6) is that for every prime p, every jointly continuous action of ℤₚ on such a manifold has nonzero kernel, so it factors through a finite quotient of ℤₚ. The group statement is then deduced from this via the classical Hilbert–Smith reduction, which the manuscript cites to Pardon (2013) rather than proving. The argument runs as follows. (i) Newman's periodicity theorem reduces to a faithful, orientation-preserving action of an open copy of ℤₚ on a connected invariant open subset O of one chart in ℝⁿ (Prop. 'chart-reduction', §5). (ii) For an odd d > n, O × ℝ^(d−n) is compactified, the orbit space Y is formed, and a degree-one map a: Y → Sᵈ is averaged out (§5). (iii) For each finite partition of the group of p-power roots of unity, integral classes z_i(t) are defined in a Witt group E_d(X) of real sheaf complexes generated by proper direct images of constant sheaves on finite polyhedra, using eigensheaf projectors of the orbit sheaf (§6). (iv) Σ_i z_i(t) = 2[A_t, α_t] and the classes are covariant and homotopy invariant (§6). (v) Finite quotient sheets plus a degree-s map that is constant off a region force all m = pᵏ classes z_i(a) to have equal rational images, which are then (4/m)ū_d. (vi) A fixed integrality lattice on E_d(Sᵈ), with denominator L_d = 2^(e_d) independent of the action (thm:sphere-lattice, §4), forces 4L_d/m to be an integer, contradicting m = pᵏ > 4L_d. The lattice is obtained by comparing the Witt groups of semialgebraic and continuous sheaf complexes with a bounded exponent-2 comparison (§4), using a dense-doubling homomorphism (thm:dense-doubling, §3) that the manuscript proves itself.
entries.delivers: If correct, it establishes the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in the restricted form stated in its theorem: for second-countable Hausdorff locally compact groups acting faithfully and jointly continuously on connected, second-countable, Hausdorff manifolds without boundary of any finite dimension, the group is a Lie group. It also gives the ℤₚ exclusion for the same class of manifolds, which is the input the list's own reduction (via Gleason–Yamabe and Newman) needs. The manuscript's abstract presents this as a proof of the conjecture 'in every finite dimension', and the introduction calls it 'a positive resolution in every positive finite dimension'. The statement of the list does not match the statement proved. The list does not assume the group is second-countable; the manuscript does. The list does not assume the manifold is connected, second-countable, or without boundary; the manuscript assumes all three. Dimension is handled as the standard finite-dimensional convention. So the result proves the conjecture for the restricted class, and says nothing about groups or manifolds outside it.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the following parts of the list's problem are still open. (a) Locally compact groups that are not second-countable (the text assumes second-countability throughout the group argument). (b) Topological manifolds that are not second-countable; the long line is a connected, Hausdorff, 1-dimensional topological manifold outside the class treated. (c) Manifolds with boundary; the theorem states 'without boundary'. (d) Disconnected manifolds; the theorem assumes connectedness and the text gives no reduction from the disconnected case. The problem_asks clause (1), about all locally compact groups with no Hausdorff or second-countability assumption, and clause (2), about all topological manifolds, are therefore only partly addressed.
entries.direction: proves a restricted case: the conjecture for second-countable groups acting on connected, second-countable, boundaryless manifolds (presented by the authors as the conjecture in every finite dimension)
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis beyond the stated restrictions, but the text relies on several results it cites rather than proves. (1) Newman's theorem on periodic homeomorphisms (Newman 1931; the modern statement is cited to Pardon 2019, 'author manuscript'). (2) The classical Hilbert–Smith reduction from locally compact groups to ℤₚ, cited to Pardon 2013, Introduction; the proof of the group statement uses it without proof. (3) Serre's results on odd spheres (Serre 1951, 1953): finiteness of higher homotopy groups, and the statement that a degree-2q map kills an element of order q; these drive the odd-sphere lemma. (4) Balmer–Walter 2002, Theorem 2.1, for the Witt localization sequence. (5) Hardt 1980 and Hardt–Lambrechts–Turchin–Volić 2011 for semialgebraic triviality and cohomology finiteness. (6) Woolf 2008 for the interval argument. (7) Dranishnikov–Ferry–Weinberger 2003 for the telescope argument. (8) Schapira's notes, Kashiwara–Schapira, Verdier, Stacks Project, and Bergfalk–Lupini–Panagiotopoulos for sheaf-theoretic foundations. Hornbostel–Schlichting's cofinality theorem is cited for the dense-inclusion bound, but §3 gives a direct proof (thm:dense-doubling), so it is not a dependency of the argument. No other OpenAI manuscript is cited.
entries.doubts: (1) The proof of the dense-doubling theorem (§3) derives y ⊕ y[1] ∈ 𝒜 from density by writing 'If density is expressed by a split inclusion, its cone supplies such a complement', and does not separately argue the non-split case. The exponent-2 bound used in the lattice depends on this step. (2) In the odd-sphere lemma (§5) the text says it will 'verify [the telescope's] homotopy type directly', but the key step, that a long enough product of degrees kills an element of πⱼ(Sᵈ), is compressed into a few sentences and rests on Serre's degree statement as cited. (3) The integral-signature and neutrality claims in the generic-signature proposition (§4) are argued in a few paragraphs, with local finiteness and locality of cohomology asserted from cited semialgebraic facts. (4) The appendix on duality signs says reversing the orientation or changing cone normalizations 'may negate both entries', and only one convention is fixed. The text does not check the main contradiction under other normalizations. (5) The text calls the result 'a positive resolution' of the conjecture. The theorem carries hypotheses (second-countable group, connected, second-countable, boundaryless manifold) that the classical statement does not, and the text does not discuss the excluded cases. (6) The claim is very strong: a dimension-free resolution with no regularity assumption, where the introduction itself describes earlier partial results that needed low dimension, regularity, or symplectic hypotheses. The decisive integrality step is a few pages long and depends on the compressed steps above.
